title: TileMapLayer CPU performance degrades on repeat runs in Editor
body:
### Tested versions

Tested in Godot Engine v4.6.stable.official, on my 2021 M1 MacBook Pro.

Encountered this when measuring performance of my MultiRect PR, but determined the issue exists outside of my changes.

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.2.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 Max (Apple7) - Apple M1 Max (10 threads) - 64.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

In editor, running a scene with a performance intensive large TileMapLayer performs worse on repeated launches.

Forward + Renderer, on my target scene: 
* Initial run from Editor averages 10 CPU ms per frame.
* Repeated runs from editor average 14 CPU ms per frame.

Compatibility Renderer, on my target scene:
* Initial run from Editor averages 26 CPU ms per frame.
* Repeated runs from editor average 37 CPU ms per frame.

In both renderers, running the scene for the first time from a fresh restart of the editor performs better than subsequent runs, and every run that is not the first seems to take the same performance hit. Something must be 'persisting' across started/stopped scenes that makes every repeat perform worse than the first.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Editor
2. Run Current Scene with a CPU intensive tilemap Scene
3. Observe CPU Frame time with Profiler
4. Stop running current scene
5. Run current Scene again
6. Observe degraded CPU Frame Time performance.
7. Stop running current scene
8. Restart the editor
9. Run Current Scene
10. Observe fresh restart produces better performance.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[batch_test_text.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25699666/batch_test_text.zip) - See Tiles.tscn, displaying a 1.8 Million Tile TileMapLayer
